activities.title: Press with cover
activities.setup: Mark 24×18m with two gates at each end. Attackers begin on the bottom half; D1/D2 start in the top half. C serves to an attacker. Attackers score through a top gate; defenders regain and counter through a bottom gate. The nearest defender engages while the other protects the route inside. Play 20–30-second possessions then reset; alternate which attacker receives. Swap pairs after four starts. End each repetition on a goal, ball out, controlled regain or the stated limit. Recover walking; retrieve only when play has stopped. Rotate the outfield roles as specified. A specialist goalkeeper stays in goal unless another suitably prepared goalkeeper is available within the stated player total. The coach serves and observes unless explicitly acting as the opponent.
activities.points: Nearest defender influences the carrier. Second defender provides cover at a distance that permits recovery. Check: The defenders name and exchange pressing/covering roles.
activities.progression: Easier: attackers start closer together. Harder: allow a wider attacking start.

Limit actions to 15 seconds then reset. Rotate the attacker and both defenders after three starts; keep all five players involved through the waiting roles.

End each repetition on a goal, ball out, controlled regain or the stated limit. Recover walking; retrieve only when play has stopped. Rotate the outfield roles as specified. A specialist goalkeeper stays in goal unless another suitably prepared goalkeeper is available within the stated player total. The coach serves and observes unless explicitly acting as the opponent.
coaching: D1 slows the attack so D2 can provide cover.
After regaining, create a passing angle rather than both running at the gate.
adaptations: Easier: delay D2 until A1 enters the final third.
Harder: D2 starts active from the first pass.
detail.success: The defenders cooperate and choose a controlled counter.

source.section: 1v1 progressing to 1v2, emphasising pressure, cover and transition.
source.adaptation: STAR uses three attackers and two defenders in the final game, no goalkeeper and cone gates. Waiting roles, entry triggers and later 3v2 phases are specified below; larger game phases are excluded.

activities.title: Water, recovery and reset
activities.setup: Stop play and secure the balls. Offer water and a comfortable break. Ask the player what she has noticed, then demonstrate the next setup. Move markers during this block so the session clock includes the transition.
activities.points: Check readiness before restarting. A longer break is always available; shorten the next block to keep the finish time.
activities.progression: Use a visual demonstration or a choice of two answers. Keep this a recovery block.

Three attackers try to reach a top gate; the two defenders protect the central route, delay and regain. On regain, both defenders attack the bottom gate against the three recovering opponents. End after 25 seconds or an outcome; rotate the defending pair each block so all players practise both phases. End each repetition on a goal, ball out, controlled regain or the stated limit. activities.points: Defenders avoid being split by one pass. The ball winner’s teammate provides a forward or supporting angle. Check: The pair recognises when to delay and when a regain is available.
activities.progression: Easier: use a 22m width to help the attackers initially. Harder for defenders: restart from an unexpected side.

activities.title: Continuous transition waves
activities.setup: Keep 3v2 and the same gates. Everyone remains live after regains until a score or ball out. Start with the three attackers towards the top. When defenders regain, the direction reverses for that possession. If the original attackers regain again, they attack the top once more. Use 90-second games with a full recovery minute. Change the pair each block. The coach adds no extra player and uses only one live ball. End each repetition on a goal, ball out, controlled regain or the stated limit. Recover walking; retrieve only when play has stopped. Rotate the outfield roles as specified. A specialist goalkeeper stays in goal unless another suitably prepared goalkeeper is available within the stated player total. The coach serves and observes unless explicitly acting as the opponent.
activities.points: Look forward, then decide whether the route is useful. Recover into positions that protect the next threat after a loss. Check: Both teams react to possession changes and use a suitable forward route.
activities.progression: Easier: pause briefly on each regain to identify direction. Harder: keep play continuous and remove coach reminders.

activities.title: Settle, reflect and take it into a match
activities.setup: Use gentle walking and easy touches. Ask: which cue helped, when would this happen in your position, and what will you try in your next club session? Each player names or demonstrates one moment. Record a short non-sensitive coaching note later in the player record.
activities.points: Compare with the player’s own starting point. Notice the decision as well as the outcome. Agree one achievable next action.
activities.progression: Let players demonstrate, point to a diagram or talk privately. Reduce extra explanation when the player is tired.
